title: Local Agglomeration and Household Mortgage Debt
eligible_reason: The paper's main regressor is the continuous local-agglomeration ratio (not a DiD). The DiD in Table 4, Panel A uses a binary state-level shock: post = 1 from the first year in which the household's state experienced intensive IPO activity (top-decile IPO intensity), with state and year fixed effects and household repeated cross-sections (SIPP) assigned to states. In the regression sample (main_code.do lines 106-117, verified with pandas on base_reg.dta merged to IPO_shock.dta) treated states adopt in 1987 (3 states, treated from the first sample year), 1991 (2), 1993 (7), 1995 (1), 1996 (2) and 2001 (1), and 24 states are never treated, so the staggered design qualifies. However, both DiD columns include the eleven time-varying controls in $x1, and the only other DiD columns are a stacked regression (Table 4B cols 1-2) and placebo/pseudo-post tests (Table 4B cols 3-6). No reported column satisfies the no-controls rule, so the paper is a near-miss.
design_notes: Data: base_reg.dta, 41,366 household observations (h_id unique per row: repeated cross-section), years 1984-2003 (SIPP topical-module years), 43 states. Merge m:1 state year with IPO_shock.dta (state-year ipo_intensity, ipo_shock; 1987-2003; 47 states), keep(3): regression sample 34,265 households in years 1987, 1988, 1991, 1993, 1995-2003. year_effective = min(year if ipo_shock==1) by state within the merged sample; post = (year >= year_effective), 0 for never-shocked states (Stata missing comparison). Table 4A: reghdfe loghh_fmort_prin post $x1, absorb(state year), vce(cluster state); same for prin_dum. Table 4B cols 1-2: stacking_data.dta with absorb(state#group_id year#group_id), cluster group_id#state. Table 4B cols 3-4: Pseudo_post = time_to_treat >= -3 (anticipation placebo); cols 5-6: Pseudo_post from randomly assigned Pseudo_year. Remaining tables use the continuous ratio, IV (PNTR trade shock), MSA-level HMDA data, interactions, subsamples.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Cohorts in the merged regression sample: 1987 (3 states, no pre-period because 1987 is the first merged year), 1991 (2), 1993 (7), 1995 (1), 1996 (2), 2001 (1); 24 never-treated states. Five cohorts have both pre and post observations.
modern_estimator_note: Stacked DiD (Table 4B cols 1-2) is the only alternative estimator; the package cites Baker, Larcker and Wang 2022 and Cengiz et al. 2019 per full-text flags.

specs.unit_var: state (assignment unit); h_id (household, one observation each)
specs.controls: hh_size hhnum_kid hhead_married hhead_female hhead_education hhead_age hhead_unemploy loghh_income_monthly hh_networth_exc_home ln_pop gdp_growth ($x1: 9 household-level and 2 state-level time-varying controls)
specs.sample_condition: base_reg merged m:1 to IPO_shock on state year, keep matched (years 1987-2003 with SIPP coverage)
specs.notes: Near-miss: dropping $x1 yields an eligible TWFE that can be run from the shipped data, but it is not reported.

ineligible_specs_note: Tables 2, 3, 5-9 use the continuous ratio (local agglomeration), IV, HMDA MSA-level data, or interactions and are outside the DiD design.
data_files: data/base_reg.dta (17 MB; 41,366 households x 69 vars; SIPP-derived)
data_files_note: All analysis files for the DiD (base_reg.dta, IPO_shock.dta) are present; README restricts use to replication. Underlying SIPP and CPS are public; IPO data from Thomson New Issues.
software_notes: Stata/SE 15; reghdfe 6.x, ftools, ivreghdfe, asdoc, estout.
priority_note: Near-miss (controls in every DiD column). A no-controls TWFE of loghh_fmort_prin / prin_dum on post with state and year FE can be run from the shipped data if the lead admits near-miss variants.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). Cohort structure verified with pandas by reproducing the merge and year_effective construction. Household data are a repeated cross-section (each h_id appears once), assigned to the state of work. The 1987 cohort has no pre-period in the merged sample (always-treated).
